core_obligations: Identify the augmentation ideal of the symmetric algebra and its square, so that the conormal module is the given module (proof lines 2117-2122).
In the smooth case apply the criterion on the conormal module of a smooth algebra to conclude that the module is finite projective (proof lines 2122-2124).
Conversely, use projectivity to split a surjection onto the module, so that the symmetric algebra is finitely presented (proof lines 2125-2130).
Apply the cotangent computation of the same section to see that the naive cotangent complex is quasi-isomorphic to the module placed in degree zero, and conclude smoothness (proof lines 2130-2136).
proof_roadmap: Projective implies finitely presented symmetric algebra (proof lines 2125-2130).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises smoothness of the symmetric algebra of a module by finite projectivity of that module, and the proof is a 20-line argument using the cotangent complex. One direction identifies the module with the quotient of the augmentation ideal by its square and applies the criterion that a smooth algebra over a ring has finite projective conormal module; the other direction chooses a surjection onto a finite projective module, uses projectivity to split it and hence to make the symmetric algebra finitely presented, and then applies the cotangent computation of the same section to show that the naive cotangent complex is concentrated in degree zero, which is smoothness. Both directions are carried out in the source and the cotangent computation is the pivot.
